sla_negotiation_notes: Customer requested uptime 99.99% for primary region; Redwood proposed 99.95% with escalated support and quicker credit schedule — negotiation ongoing

Credit schedule points: OmniWave wants credits triggered by any calendar-hour downtime > 0.5% leading to pro rata credits up to 100% of that hour. Redwood prefers monthly cap (max 50% monthly invoice) + progressive credit tiers (minor outage 5-10%, prolonged 25-50%). Need legal redline.

Latency SLOs: customer requires P95 <= 150ms for small prompt paths and P99 <= 300ms; Redwood suggests P95 <= 180ms for first 3 months after cutover while prefix cache warms. Customer pushing for firm SLO with performance credits tied to SLO breaches.

Maintenance windows: OmniWave requests no scheduled maintenance in 00:00-08:00 local core TZ (NA East) and max one 2-hour maintenance per month. Redwood default: monthly 4-hour window with 72h notice. Compromise proposed: 2x2h windows with 7d notice and emergency maintenance carve-outs.

Support / response times: OmniWave requires Sev1 initial response <= 15 minutes and live on-call contact; Redwood current enterprise SLA: Sev1 1 hour, Sev2 4 hours. SE/AE proposing 30 min initial response + dedicated pager for first 90 days of ramp.

Reserved GPU planning: initial commit 8xA100-equivalent sustained, ability to burst to 12 for 30min sustained per hour. Need confirmation from capacity team on GPU pool tenancy and isolation guarantees.
Telemetry & audits: OmniWave requires daily token-level usage reports and a monthly latency distribution export. Redwood to provide token breakdown and tracing hooks via console + S3 export option.
Legal wants explicit exclusion list for force majeure and maintenance; Customer pushing for narrower exclusions. Redlines expected from both sides (see linked_drive_docs).
